sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Algonquin, Illinois?
sections.html:
Algonquin is a Fox River suburb about 40 miles northwest of the Chicago Loop, and a sale there means working with two counties because the village straddles the McHenry and Kane line. Roughly 78 percent of the village area is in McHenry County and the rest is in Kane County, so the county printed on your tax bill decides who records the deed and who collects the tax.

The place grew slowly for a long time. The name became official on December 23, 1847, a railroad arrived in 1855, and the village was formed on February 25, 1890. Summer homes along the river made it a weekend getaway for Chicago families for much of the twentieth century. The population then climbed from 5,684 in 1980 to 11,663 in 1990 and 23,276 in 2000, which means most of the housing is relatively young. The 2020 count was 29,700 and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 30,824.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024: $351,000
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 88.2%
  • Median gross rent: $1,723
  • Median household income: $134,525
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher: 43.6%
  • Mean travel time to work: 30.6 minutes

sections.h2: Which parts of Algonquin shape what a buyer is willing to pay?
sections.html:
Location inside the village matters because Algonquin has distinct districts with different traffic and different housing. Old Town sits along Main Street (Illinois Route 31) near the original village hall at 2 South Main Street, and exterior changes to any building in its historic district need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the village.

The Randall Road corridor on the western side is the retail spine. Algonquin Commons, an outdoor mall of about 80 stores, opened in 2004, and the Algonquin Corporate Campus was planned across more than 1,000 acres between Randall Road and Square Barn Road. The manufacturing belt runs along Algonquin Road between Pyott Road and Route 31, west of Old Town, and it houses tool, die, mold and plastics shops.

Subdivision names that show up in school boundary descriptions include Willoughby Farms, Brittany Hills, Providence Point and Shenandoah. A buyer comparing a house near the industrial belt with one near the river will weigh noise and truck traffic differently, so an honest description in the listing or cash offer discussion saves time later.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Algonquin houses?
sections.html:
Two districts split the village, and the boundary often decides which houses draw the most interest from families. Community Unit School District 300 covers the area generally along and east of Randall Road. Consolidated School District 158, headquartered in Algonquin, serves the far western side.

  • District 300 elementary schools serving the village include Neubert, Eastview and Algonquin Lakes, plus Lincoln Prairie and Lake in the Hills Elementary in neighboring towns.
  • Westfield Community School serves the Willoughby Farms area and feeds Jacobs High School. Algonquin Middle School serves Eastview and Algonquin Lakes and feeds mostly into Dundee-Crown High School.
  • District 158 runs Mackeben Elementary, Marion Conley Elementary and Bernice Heinemann Middle School on the Square Barn Road campus, with Huntley High School for high school.
  • St. Margaret Mary Catholic School and Foundations Montessori School are the private options.

McHenry County College generally serves residents in the District 158 boundaries, while Elgin Community College serves residents in District 300.

sections.h2: Do I need a village permit before repairing or selling an Algonquin house?
sections.html:
Algonquin requires a building permit before anyone erects, enlarges, alters, repairs, moves, improves, removes, converts or demolishes a building or structure. Small cosmetic jobs are listed as exceptions. The Community Development Department says permit review can take up to five weeks, so repairs you want done before listing should start early.

Permit status for common jobs, from the Village of Algonquin permit information page

Source: Village of Algonquin, Permit Information.

Anyone moving into a newly built home needs a certificate of occupancy before move-in. The village adopted the 2018 International Residential Code and the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code, among others. Questions go to Community Development at (847) 658-2700, option 3, or permits@algonquin.org. If a prior owner finished a basement or deck, ask that office whether the permit was closed before you list.

sections.h2: How do roads, fire districts and transit affect an Algonquin address?
sections.html:
The road network is the first thing out-of-town buyers check. Randall Road is the multi-lane north and south arterial and runs six lanes for the stretch between Harnish Drive and Corporate Parkway. Illinois Route 31 is the two-lane Main Street through downtown, and the intersection with Algonquin Road backs up at peak times. Illinois Route 25 runs along the eastern edge and ends at Route 62. Pace Route 550 runs along Randall Road between Crystal Lake and Elgin.

Fire and rescue come from one of three districts depending on the address: the Algonquin-Lake in the Hills Fire Protection District, the Huntley Fire Protection District or the Carpentersville Countryside Fire Protection District. The tax bill lists the districts that serve the parcel.

sections.h2: How is property tax billed for an Algonquin house in McHenry County?
sections.html:
McHenry County mails one bill and collects two installments. For the 2026 collection year, bills were mailed in early May and the installments were due June 9 and September 9. The Treasurer's Office is at 2100 N. Seminary Ave. in Woodstock and takes payments at the window or the drive-thru lanes on weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

  • eCheck payments online carry no fee. Credit cards, debit cards and digital wallets add a 2.4% convenience fee.
  • Two 24-hour drop boxes, one walk-up and one drive-up, accept checks and money orders payable to the McHenry County Collector. No cash.
  • Write the parcel number (PIN) on any check, and ask the Post Office for a postmark when mailing close to a due date.
  • The VIP Taxpayer program sends email and text reminders and lets owners switch to e-billing.

Parcels in the Kane County part of the village are billed by Kane County, so look at the county name on the bill before you pay. At closing, ask the title officer to settle the current year's tax and any open installment between buyer and seller.

sections.h2: What does McHenry County want on a deed recorded for an Algonquin sale?
sections.html:
The County Recorder rejects documents that miss formatting or content rules, and a rejection can push back the date a buyer gets title. The Recorder's tips page asks for a white 20-pound page with a half-inch clean margin on every side and a clear 3 by 5 inch space in the upper right corner.

  • A deed needs the grantor's signature, the grantee's address and the full McHenry County legal description.
  • A Plat Act affidavit must accompany the deed when the legal description is metes and bounds.
  • Either a completed exemption paragraph or the Illinois transfer declaration (PTAX-203 or MyDec) must accompany every deed. A MyDec filing must state "Closing Completed."
  • Every document needs "Prepared By" and "Mail To" lines with names and addresses.

The state transfer tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value stated in the declaration under 35 ILCS 200/31-10. Ask the McHenry or Kane County Recorder, whichever holds your parcel, for any county stamp and for the Rental Housing Support Program surcharge details.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house quickly in Algonquin?
sections.html:
Sellers in Algonquin generally choose between a traditional listing, a private sale and an as-is purchase by a cash buyer. A listing suits a house that is move-in ready. A private sale saves agent costs but leaves the permit, deed and declaration work to the owner and the closing attorney. A cash purchase fits a vacant, inherited or tenant-occupied house that needs work, since the buyer takes it in the condition it is in.

Whichever route you pick, an open permit or a missing certificate of occupancy will still come up at closing, so a call to Community Development early in the process keeps the schedule intact.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Algonquin deed and tax bill?
faqs.a: It depends on the parcel. About 78 percent of the village is in McHenry County and the remainder is in Kane County. The county name on your tax bill tells you whom to ask.

faqs.q: Does Algonquin require a permit for a small roof repair?
faqs.a: Not for a repair of 200 square feet or less. Larger roof work, gutters and downspouts, and a garage service door do need permits.

faqs.q: When were McHenry County property tax installments due in 2026?
faqs.a: June 9 and September 9, 2026. Check the Treasurer's Office for the dates on the next bill, and pay online by eCheck to avoid the 2.4% fee charged on cards.

faqs.q: Does Algonquin Old Town have extra rules for exterior work?
faqs.a: Yes. A Certificate of Appropriateness is required for all exterior changes, additions and demolitions to buildings inside the historic district.

faqs.q: What must a MyDec filing say for McHenry County recording?
faqs.a: It must state "Closing Completed." The Recorder also needs the grantee's address, the legal description and a Plat Act affidavit if the description is metes and bounds.
